text:
If one dwells in internal emptiness, one is practicing the manifestation of that internal emptiness, but one is not practicing the <term>Prajnaparamita</term> <gloss>Perfection of Wisdom</gloss>. Blessed One, if a <term>Bodhisattva Mahasattva</term> <gloss>a great being dedicated to awakening</gloss>, while practicing the <term>Prajnaparamita</term>, dwells in external emptiness with a mind that remains attached to the concepts of self and belonging due to a lack of skillful means, then one is practicing the manifestation of that external emptiness, but one is not practicing the <term>Prajnaparamita</term>. Blessed

<summary>This passage explains that dwelling on the concepts of internal and external emptiness without skillful means constitutes a conceptual attachment rather than the true practice of the Perfection of Wisdom.</summary>
<keywords>Prajnaparamita, emptiness, Bodhisattva, skillful means, non-attachment</keywords>
